pbscn_: Oskar Pbscn reported to S-F11 with a key to a house that is no longer there sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
Oskar Pbscn was in the first hundred. The old hands in S-F11 call them 'the early birds', and not always kindly.

Oskar Pbscn waited at the fire step while a flare burned out. The pale shape beyond the wire resolved into a sack, exactly where the sack had always been. Word came down the line: Verdel Ridge is ours. Oskar Pbscn shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Oskar Pbscn stood at the parapet at dawn with the rest of S-F11, bayonet fixed, staring into the grey. Nothing came. Nothing came yesterday, either.
A borrowed towel came back cleaner than when Oskar Pbscn lent it. He is considering lending out the rest of the washing.
Oskar Pbscn cut Marek Jackmdunn's hair with a bayonet and a cracked mirror. It is not good. It is, however, short.
vl.tsanev: Clement Tsanev left his mother, who writes every Sunday behind in Lindenbruck and came up the line with a lock of hair in a matchbox. The men noticed at once that he keeps feeding the rats.
As one of the first hundred volunteers, Clement Tsanev received the First Wave ribbon. A neighbour lent the needle and supervised every stitch.
Clement Tsanev found water collecting beneath the gun's cover. He sketched a small shelter and took the drawing to the stores.

The stores supplied Clement Tsanev with shorter boards than requested. The gun shelter has become an exercise in joints and bad language. Verdel Ridge fell to the Concord at dusk. Clement Tsanev helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
Clement Tsanev finished the shelter. The crew tested every movement of the gun and discovered that the roof needed moving back a hand's width.
Clement Tsanev taught Emil Majormalprac to play the harmonica. The whole squad has asked them both, politely, to stop.
Clement Tsanev fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Walter Mat, badly wounded. Nobody nearby said anything.
